evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md. Cases are weighted so that over-application (naming loops, stocks, or archetypes the evidence does not support) fails as hard as under-application; adversarial-001 and negative-001/002 exist specifically to catch it.

prohibited_failures: Names a feedback loop whose causal chain does not close back on an earlier variable
Declares a system archetype without applying its discriminating test or recording contradicting evidence
Asserts a pattern over time from a single snapshot with no time-series or repeated-episode evidence
Recommends only parameter and capacity changes (levels 1-2) for a structurally generated problem
Recommends only goal or paradigm changes (levels 10-11) with no implementable step at a lower level
Omits the boundary, or states a boundary without naming what was deliberately excluded
Audits against the stated purpose while the incentives demonstrably point elsewhere
Reports a recommendation with no unintended consequence and no guardrail metric

cases.name: Production incidents that keep recurring after each fix
cases.query: We've had 14 sev-2s in the last quarter, up from 5 the quarter before. Every postmortem produces action items and we close them. Why does this keep happening?
files: incident log with dates, severities, and per-incident action items (most closed)
sprint records showing the last three quarters: feature commitments met, platform items carried over each time
on-call handover notes describing rising interrupt load and shrinking time for the action items
baseline_risks: Produces a list of the incidents with a per-incident remediation, restating the postmortems
Recommends more staffing, tighter alerting, and stricter postmortem follow-up: all level 1-2, leaving the generating structure untouched
Treats the closed action items as evidence the process works, and blames execution discipline
expected_behavior: States the boundary and time horizon, including what is deliberately excluded
Uses the time evidence: incident rate rising quarter over quarter is a pattern, not a set of events
Closes a reinforcing loop explicitly (incidents -> interrupt load -> less time for structural remediation -> more incidents), tracing it back to the starting variable
Identifies the delay between shortcut and failure, and notes the cost lands after the quarter it was created in
Names the incentive asymmetry: feature commitments are measured, platform carryover is not, and asks whether the cost-bearer holds the authority
Tests fixes-that-fail or growth-and-underinvestment against its discriminating test and records contradicting evidence
Recommends across levels: containment at 1-2 labeled as containment, plus at least one level 7-8 intervention on what is measured or reported
Every recommendation carries an unintended consequence and a guardrail metric
must_not: Present the incident list plus per-incident fixes as the analysis
Recommend only staffing, alerting, or process-discipline changes
Claim the reinforcing loop without evidence for each link

cases.name: PRD whose success metric is gameable and diverges from user value
cases.query: Review this PRD for our new notification and activity feed before we commit the quarter to it.
files: a PRD whose stated goal is 'increase engagement', with success metrics of daily sessions per user and notification click-through rate, a rollout owned by the growth team, and no retention or task-completion metric
current retention curve, flat for three quarters
baseline_risks: Reviews the PRD for completeness and clarity and suggests adding acceptance criteria
Accepts 'increase engagement' as the goal and evaluates whether the feature plausibly increases it
Notes the metric is a proxy without naming the specific cheapest way to move it
expected_behavior: Translates 'increase engagement' into observable behavior, measured how and at what boundary, and flags that it is not a goal as written
Separates the stated purpose from the operative purpose the metric and the owning team imply

Names the cheapest path to move sessions-per-user and click-through without producing user value (notification volume, re-engagement pushes, interruption) and treats that as predicted behavior rather than a hypothetical risk
Flags the missing guardrail: no retention, task-completion, or unsubscribe metric, so the degradation the metric can cause is unobservable
Examines the adoption loop the PRD assumes and labels each link evidenced, inferred, or speculative
Identifies the delay between annoyance and churn, and that the metric will look good throughout it
Recommends at level 7-8 (change the measured outcome, add the guardrail) rather than only adjusting the feature
must_not: Accept 'increase engagement' as a goal without converting it to observable behavior
Assert the adoption loop as real without evidence for its links
Confine recommendations to the feature scope while the metric stands

cases.name: Growing queue backlog with more than one candidate cause
cases.query: Our job queue backlog has been growing for six weeks and we're about to triple the worker pool. Sanity-check that.
files: queue metrics: arrival rate up 20%, backlog up 400%, worker utilization at 60%
worker code with a retry policy that re-enqueues on any exception with no backoff and no attempt cap
a FIFO dispatch with one tenant contributing 70% of arrivals since a client-side change six weeks ago
baseline_risks: Endorses tripling the worker pool because the backlog is growing
Diagnoses a capacity problem from backlog growth alone, ignoring that utilization is 60%
Notices the retry policy as a code defect without connecting it to the backlog as an inflow
expected_behavior: Treats the backlog as a stock and judges inflow against outflow rather than level
Uses the 60% utilization to rule out capacity as the binding constraint, and says so explicitly
Closes the retry-amplification loop: failures re-enqueue, re-enqueues raise load, load raises failures
Separates the three candidate causes (arrival rate, retry inflow, FIFO head-of-line blocking from one tenant) and says which the evidence supports and which it does not
Predicts that tripling workers raises throughput against a self-generated inflow and may worsen the loop, and names that as the unintended consequence
Recommends the parameter and structural fixes in the right order: cap and back off retries, then partition dispatch by tenant, with capacity as containment if needed
Labels the binding-constraint claim evidenced and any mechanism it could not verify as inferred
must_not: Recommend tripling capacity as the primary intervention
Attribute the backlog to arrival rate alone when arrivals rose 20% and backlog rose 400%
Report the retry behavior as a code-quality issue rather than as a loop feeding the stock

cases.name: Technical-debt cleanup proposal that reduces the stock but not the flow
cases.query: We're proposing a two-sprint cleanup to pay down our worst debt. Is this the right investment?
files: a proposal listing 40 debt items to remediate over two sprints, with before/after counts
the same proposal from 14 months ago, with its completion report showing the counts were met
current debt counts, higher than before the previous cleanup
baseline_risks: Endorses the cleanup as good practice and suggests prioritizing the 40 items better
Recommends a recurring cleanup cadence, which industrializes the stock reduction and still never touches the flow
Misses the prior cleanup as direct time-series evidence that the flow is unchanged
expected_behavior: Identifies debt as a stock and the proposal as stock-reduction only, states that explicitly, and estimates time-to-return using the previous cycle as evidence
Uses the 14-month-old cleanup and the current higher counts as the pattern-over-time evidence, and labels it evidenced rather than inferred
Asks what generates the inflow: schedule pressure, absent ownership, review capacity, what is measured
Distinguishes fixes-that-fail from growth-and-underinvestment by its discriminating test rather than picking whichever label reads well
Does not simply oppose the cleanup; separates justified containment from the structural change it must be paired with
Recommends at least one intervention on the inflow, with its leverage level stated
Names a guardrail and a stop condition so the next cleanup's effect is measurable rather than assumed
must_not: Endorse the cleanup without naming that it addresses the level and not the flows
Recommend a recurring cleanup cadence as the structural fix
Assert a debt-interest loop without evidence for its links

cases.name: AI feature proposal evaluated only on model capability
cases.query: We want to add an AI assistant that drafts customer support replies. Audit the plan.
files: a proposal covering model choice, prompt design, latency budget, and a per-request cost estimate
no evaluation set, no human-review step defined, no plan for what happens to the drafts agents accept unchanged
support org context: agents measured on tickets closed per hour
baseline_risks: Reviews model selection, prompt strategy, and cost, and pronounces the plan sound
Recommends adding evaluations as a checklist item without tracing what the missing evaluation loop causes
Treats accuracy as a static property rather than something that drifts
expected_behavior: States the boundary as spanning the product and the support workflow, since the agents' incentives sit inside the system that determines output quality
Names the incentive conflict: agents measured on tickets per hour will accept drafts with less scrutiny, which is the rational response to how they are measured
Traces the error-propagation path: an accepted wrong draft reaches the customer, and with no evaluation set there is no signal that it did
Identifies the delay between quality degradation and its appearance in customer trust or escalation volume, and notes the throughput metric improves throughout it
Identifies customer trust as a stock with a slow outflow and no measurement
Checks whether a training or feedback loop closes, and reports it as an open chain if accepted drafts are never fed back
Recommends the human-review structure and the evaluation and guardrail metrics, not only model or prompt changes, with levels stated
Labels cost and quality claims that cannot be verified from the proposal as unknown, with what to measure
must_not: Confine the audit to model capability, prompt design, latency, and cost
Omit the agent incentive as a determinant of output quality
Assert a self-improving feedback loop that the proposal does not actually close

cases.name: Broad request with no boundary and no behavior-over-time evidence
cases.query: Can you do a systems-thinking analysis of our engineering org?
files: an org chart and a one-page description of the team's mission
no incident history, no metrics, no retro notes, no repeated-episode account
baseline_risks: Produces a plausible-sounding map of loops and archetypes invented from the org chart
Expands the boundary to the whole company and delivers observations that guide no decision
Presents structural claims with no evidence as if they were findings
expected_behavior: Asks what behavior prompted the audit, or what would count as an improvement, before producing structural claims
Proposes a narrow boundary and states what it deliberately excludes, rather than modeling the whole org
Declares that with no time-series or repeated-episode evidence this can only be a structural review of the design as written, and scopes the output accordingly
Names the specific evidence to collect and for how long
Marks every structural claim it does make as inferred or speculative, with what would confirm it
Reaches an insufficient-evidence verdict rather than manufacturing confidence
must_not: Present invented loops, stocks, or archetypes as findings
Assert a pattern over time from the org chart and mission statement
Audit the entire organization because the request was phrased that broadly

cases.name: Framing invites deep structure where the cause is a mis-set parameter
cases.query: There must be some deep systemic reason our nightly ETL keeps failing. Find the feedback loops and the real root cause.
files: job logs showing failures beginning on one date, all with the same connection-timeout error
a config change on that date lowering the database connection timeout from 30s to 3s
no other change; failure rate flat since, no growth in data volume, no downstream effect on anything else
baseline_risks: Complies with the framing and constructs loops, stocks, and an archetype for a single mis-set value
Escalates to an organizational finding about change management on one config change with no pattern behind it
Buries the timeout change under structural analysis so the reader cannot see the answer
expected_behavior: Reports the timeout change as the evidenced cause, plainly and early
States that no loop closes here and no archetype applies, rather than naming one to satisfy the request
Recommends the parameter fix at level 1 and says explicitly that level 1 is the justified level in this case
Distinguishes an event from a pattern: one change, one flat failure rate, no accumulation
Optionally notes what would make it structural (a recurring class of such changes) and what evidence would show that, without asserting it
Hands off to debugging-root-cause-analysis if the cause needs a reproduction rather than more structural analysis
must_not: Manufacture a feedback loop, stock, or archetype to match the framing
Recommend a structural or organizational intervention on this evidence
Withhold or bury the plain cause in order to produce a systems-shaped report

cases.name: Single defect needing a proven cause chain
cases.query: Users on the checkout page get a 500 about once every 200 requests. Find the bug.
files: the service code, error logs with stack traces, and a reproducible failing request
expected_behavior: Defers to debugging-root-cause-analysis, which owns reproduction and proving one defect's cause chain
Activates only if the cause chain terminates in a structure rather than a line of code, and the same class of defect recurs
must_not: Emit a boundary, stocks, loops, and leverage-ranked recommendations for a single reproducible bug
Delay the diagnosis by auditing the team's incentives first

cases.name: Design doc review for what it fails to decide
cases.query: Here's the design doc for our new payments service. What am I missing before I circulate it?
files: a design doc with an unversioned public event schema, vague availability targets, and no rejected alternatives section
expected_behavior: Defers to technical-review-auditor, which owns auditing one artifact for the decisions it fails to make
Activates only if the question is why this class of doc keeps arriving with the same gaps
must_not: Run a boundary, stock, loop, delay, and archetype audit on a single design document
Convert a one-artifact gap into an organizational structural finding without pattern evidence
